content.text: Root cause: the "no closer after here" cache is global and is set by whichever scan reached the end of the input. Its validity only covers openers at or after that scan's start. When a link label scan runs ahead, reaches the end, and then fails, the earlier backtick is re-parsed and wrongly trusts the cache. I'll record the earliest position the end-reaching scan covered and only use the cache for openers at or after it.

content.text:
The bug is fixed: a valid code span after an unclosed `[` or `![` now renders as a code span, matching the CommonMark reference output. **Cause:** `src/rules_inline/backticks.ts` caches "no closing backtick after here" in a global flag and a per-length table. That cache was filled by whichever scan reached the end of the input, which can be a scan that started at a later backtick. When a link label scan runs ahead and then fails, the parser re-reads the earlier backtick and trusts the cache for a position the scan never covered. For `[`a`b`` the closer at index 1 was skipped, so the code span was dropped. **Fix:** - `src/rules_inline/state_inline.ts`: added `backticksScanStart`, the earliest opener position whose scan reached the end of the input. - `src/rules_inline/backticks.ts`: the cache is used only for openers at or after that position, and each end-reaching scan lowers it to its own start. **Verification:** - Before the fix, `[foo `bar` baz``, `![alt `code` x``, `[`a`b``, and `[a `b` c`` all rendered as literal text under the commonmark and default presets. After the fix they match the reference output, e.g. `

[foo bar baz`

`. - Added three fixture cases to `test/fixtures/markdown-it/commonmark_extras.txt`: the link case, the image case, and the minimal `` [`a`b` `` trigger. - `test/markdown-it` and `test/cmspec` pass. - `tsc --noEmit` passes. - `test/build` fails with "Cannot find module … dist/markdown-it.cjs.js" because `dist/` is not built. That predates this change. I did not run `npm run build`, which would create `dist/`. - ESLint did not lint the changed files: it reported them as ignored by its config, with no errors. `npx` and `npm` commands were denied, so I ran the binaries directly. **Zero preset:** the report says the zero preset also shows the bug. It doesn't. The zero preset enables only the `text` inline rule, so it never parses backticks at all, including a plain `` `a` ``. Its literal output is by design, so I left it alone.
